Good morning, Adrian Lim. This is Rachel Koh. Is this a convenient time for our telephone discussion? Before we begin, may I have your identification details?

Good morning, Rachel. I have somewhere quiet to speak, so this is convenient. My FIN is F four one three eight two five two H. My date of birth is the fifth of November nineteen ninety-two.

Thank you. I will keep the discussion focused and leave room for any questions. Please tell me which holding you wish to discuss and the instruction you have in mind.

The holding I want to transact in is Harbor SGD Bond Fund. I want to sell from my existing holding to release liquidity. Please use Singapore dollars as the transaction currency for this order. My separate existing holding is denominated in Japanese yen; please leave that holding untouched. That is not the currency instruction for this transaction.

Your objective is to release liquidity for planned personal expenditure while reducing your exposure to fluctuations in bond valuations. That is the objective I am working to. With Harbor SGD Bond Fund, rising market interest rates can reduce the value of the underlying bonds and lower the fund's unit value. Do you understand how rising interest rates could lower the value of your holding in this fund?

Yes, I understand. Rising interest rates can lower the value of the fund's underlying bonds, which can reduce the value of my holding.

You could lose some or all of the capital you invested in this fund. Selling when its value is below what you paid would crystallise a loss. Are you willing to accept an investment loss if selling your holding crystallises that loss?

Yes, I am willing to accept that investment loss to meet my liquidity needs rather than wait for a recovery.

I recommend reducing your holding in Harbor SGD Bond Fund because it releases funds for your planned expenditure and reduces your exposure to further interest-rate and credit-driven valuation changes. You would, however, give up participation in any subsequent recovery on the portion sold.

Thank you for keeping the explanation direct. Business responsibilities have been taking up most of my diary, and I am fitting personal administration into the gaps. A concise telephone discussion is much easier to manage than a long email exchange.

For future updates, I can keep the opening brief and let you raise anything that needs more discussion. For this call, I am ready to take the remaining order details.

The monetary amount for this transaction is 100k. The quantity for the order is 500 units. Please place this as a market order.

Let me check the direction: you want to buy from this fund.

No, that is not the direction I instructed. I want to sell from my existing holding to release liquidity.

I apologise for that slip. With the direction now corrected, do you explicitly confirm the final transaction instruction, including the product, currency, amount, quantity and order type you specified, and authorise me to place it?

Yes, I confirm the final transaction instruction with my correction included, and I authorise you to place that order.

Thank you, Adrian. That concludes our discussion. I will let you get back to your day.

Thank you, Rachel. Goodbye.
